summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia status post allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. He was found to be volume overloaded with acute kidney injury and hyperuricemia, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, which improved his respiratory status and renal function. His medications were adjusted, including transitioning to twice-daily torsemide and starting allopurinol for hyperuricemia. He received IVIG during admission and remained on his baseline immunosuppressive regimen. Imaging showed resolution of prior pulmonary opacities without new infection or edema. He stabilized, was deemed safe for discharge, and returned home with close follow-up planned.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Hyperuricemia without signs of inflammatory arthritis and tophaceous disease
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Other specified disorders of the skin and subcutaneous tissue
